mainTopic: Where the עומר comes from and why, the story of the חשמונאי civil war behind the משנה's מעשה, and stories of מרדכי's wisdom.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question about a sick person who needs figs on שבת. Because one stem holding three figs means less cutting than two separate figs, we bring the three. Then a new משנה teaches that the עומר barley should ideally come from fields near ירושלים, but may come from anywhere if those fields have not ripened. The גמרא gives two reasons for preferring nearby fields: the word כרמל (the grain must be fresh), or the rule אין מעבירין על המצוות (do not pass over a מצוה). Next a ברייתא tells the story behind the משנה's מעשה. During the civil war of the חשמונאי kings, a pig was sent up the wall of ירושלים instead of an animal for the תמיד, and the חכמים cursed raising pigs and teaching חכמת יוונית. In that time of war, deaf-mutes gave hand-sign hints that מרדכי decoded to find גגות צריפין for the עומר and עין סוכר for the שתי הלחם. A final story shows מרדכי correctly reading three women's unclear words, showing that all their bird offerings were עולות.

steps.title: Even רבי ישמעאל would agree: cut the stem of three figs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי ישמעאל cut less on שבת only because eating less also meant reaping less. With the figs, two separate figs means more cutting, so everyone agrees we bring the one stem with three figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל only said his rule there because when you cut down the amount to be eaten, you also cut down the reaping. But here, if you cut down the amount to be eaten by taking two separate figs, you actually add to the reaping. So we certainly bring the three figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion. It shows that רבי ישמעאל's ruling about the עומר on שבת cannot be used to require cutting only two figs for a sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל wanted less grain reaped for the עומר on שבת, because less grain to eat also meant less reaping, which is normally a forbidden מלאכה on שבת. With figs it works the other way. Two figs on two separate stems need two cuts, while three figs on one stem need only one cut. Since the real concern is the amount of reaping, we bring the three figs.

keyTerms.meaning: "He only said it up to here": the opinion is limited to its own case
Reaping or cutting a plant, a forbidden מלאכה on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת the goal is to keep the forbidden act (reaping) as small as possible. That can matter more than keeping the amount of food small.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the point is to give the sick person as little food as possible. The goal is the fewest cuts. One stem holding three figs means fewer cuts than two separate figs.

phrases.aramaic: דְּעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָתָם,
phrases.english: For רבי ישמעאל only said there
phrases.notes: "There" means the earlier משנה about reaping the עומר on שבת.

phrases.english: because when one reduces the eating
he also reduces the reaping.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּכִי קָא מְמַעֵט בַּאֲכִילָה
phrases.english: But here, when one reduces the eating
phrases.notes: "Here" means the sick person's figs. Taking two separate figs means less food.

phrases.english: he increases the reaping,
so certainly we bring three.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a discussion that began before this section, by setting רבי ישמעאל's case apart from the figs case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי ישמעאל reduces the amount on שבת, maybe we should also bring only two figs, the smaller amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל cares about less reaping. Since two figs mean more cutting, we bring the three on one stem.

steps.title: משנה: the עומר should come from nearby fields
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says the best way to do the מצוה is to bring the עומר barley from fields close to ירושלים. If those fields have not ripened yet, it may be brought from anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of the עומר is to bring it from nearby. If the fields near ירושלים did not ripen, we bring it from any place.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the preferred place to take the עומר barley from: fields close to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. The best way to do the מצוה is to use nearby fields. Barley from far away is still valid when the nearby barley is not ready. Distance affects the best way of doing the מצוה, not whether the עומר counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule the גמרא will try to explain in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מִצְוַת הָעוֹמֶר לְהָבִיא מִן הַקָּרוֹב,
phrases.english: MISHNA: The מצוה of the omer is to bring it from nearby.
If the area near Jerusalem did not ripen,
we bring it from any place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic in a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The best choice is to take the עומר from fields near ירושלים. If they are not ripe, it may come from anywhere.

steps.title: A real case: barley and wheat brought from far away
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells of a time the עומר came from גגות צריפין and the wheat for the שתי הלחם came from בקעת עין סוכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It once happened that the עומר came from גגות צריפין, and the two loaves came from the valley of עין סוכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up its rule with a story. Offerings really were brought from places that were not the closest ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows the second half of the rule in action: when nearby grain was not ready, grain from other places was used. It also shows the same idea for the שתי הלחם of שבועות, which are made from wheat.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves offered on שבועות

phrases.english: There was an incident where the omer came from Gaggot Tzerifin,
and the two loaves from the valley of Ein Sokher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real story that shows the rule from the step before.
steps.raayaObject: That grain may be taken from farther places when nearby grain is not ready.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A historical event in the בית המקדש.

steps.title: Why should the עומר come from nearby?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule that the עומר should come from nearby fields.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking why nearby fields are preferred. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule but not its source or reason. The גמרא wants to know what lies behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the עומר should ideally be taken from fields near ירושלים.

steps.title: First answer: the grain must be fresh (כרמל)
steps.stepSummary: One answer is the word כרמל in the פסוק. It means fresh, moist grain, and grain from nearby will still be fresh when it arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because of the word "כרמל".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first possible reason, which comes from a word in the פסוק about the מנחת ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls this grain כרמל, meaning fresh and soft. A long trip could make the grain dry and hard. So it should come from close by.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you want, say": brings one possible answer, often one of two
Fresh, moist grain still full and soft

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is because of "karmel" [fresh grain].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the step before.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires fresh grain (כרמל), so it should come from nearby.

steps.title: Second answer: do not pass over a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Another answer is the rule אין מעבירין על המצוות. When you meet a chance to do a מצוה, you should not skip it. So we use the first barley we reach, which is the nearby barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is because we do not pass over מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason for the same rule. This one is based on a general principle, not a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer was about the grain itself, which must be fresh. This answer is about how we treat a מצוה. Skipping the nearby fields to go to farther ones would be passing over a מצוה that is right in front of us.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not pass over a מצוה; do the one that comes to you first

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons for using nearby barley: (1) כרמל, the grain must be fresh; (2) אין מעבירין על המצוות, do not skip a מצוה that is in front of you.
steps.whyThisMatters: אין מעבירין על המצוות is a general rule found across the תלמוד. It teaches us to grab a מצוה as soon as the chance comes.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
it is because one does not pass over the מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין מַעֲבִירִין עַל הַמִּצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate reason in place of the first answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We do not pass over a מצוה, so we take the first barley we come to, the nearby barley.

steps.title: The background: the civil war of the חשמונאי kings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's מעשה again and brings a ברייתא with its background. The חשמונאי kings הורקנוס and אריסטובלוס were at war, one outside ירושלים and one inside. Every day the people inside paid for animals for the תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's story of the עומר coming from גגות צריפין, a ברייתא teaches: when the חשמונאי kings fought each other, הורקנוס was outside the city and אריסטובלוס was inside. Every day those inside lowered coins in a box, and those outside sent up animals for the daily offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה and starts a ברייתא that tells the story behind it. This step sets the scene for what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 only said that the עומר once came from גגות צריפין. Now the גמרא tells us what was going on at that time: a siege of ירושלים during a civil war. Even during the siege, the תמיד kept being brought every day.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily תמיד offerings brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: There was an incident where the omer came from Gaggot Tzerifin.
phrases.notes: This is the line from the משנה we saw in step 3. Some versions have the word in square brackets, "the omer," and some don't.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁצָּרוּ מַלְכֵי בֵּית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי זֶה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: When the kings of the Hasmonean house besieged each other,
and Hyrcanus was outside the city
and Aristobulus was inside,

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם הָיוּ מְשַׁלְשְׁלִין לָהֶן
phrases.english: every single day they would lower down to them
dinars in a box,
and the others would send up to them animals for the daily offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבָּא הָעוֹמֶר מִגַּגּוֹת צְרִיפִין. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the מעשה quoted in step 3 and starts a ברייתא that gives its background.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the חשמונאי civil war, the people inside ירושלים paid each day for animals so the תמיד could still be brought.

steps.title: The old man's advice and the pig on the wall
steps.stepSummary: An old man who knew חכמת יוונית hinted to the besiegers that the city would not fall while the עבודה continued. The next day they sent up a pig instead of a kosher animal. When the pig dug into the wall, ארץ ישראל shook.
steps.simpleTranslation: An old man who knew Greek wisdom hinted to those outside: as long as they keep doing the Temple service, they will not fall into your hands. The next day, when the coins came down, they sent up a pig. When it reached halfway up the wall, it dug its hooves into the wall, and ארץ ישראל shook over an area of four hundred by four hundred פרסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story. An old man's secret advice leads the besiegers to send up a pig, and the whole land shakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man taught that the עבודה in the בית המקדש was protecting the city. So the besiegers tried to stop the עבודה by sending a non-kosher animal instead of a תמיד. The shaking of the land shows how terrible this act was.

keyTerms.meaning: Greek wisdom; here a special way of speaking that only people trained in it could understand
He spoke in a foreign way, hinting so others would not understand
A פרסה, a measure of distance

phrases.english: There was a certain old man there
who was familiar with Greek wisdom.
He hinted to them in the language of Greek wisdom,
he said to them:
As long as they are busy with the Temple service,
they will not be handed over to you.
The next day they lowered dinars in a box to them,
and they sent up a pig to them.
Once it reached halfway up the wall,
it dug its hooves into the wall,
and the Land of Israel shook

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה עַל אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה.
phrases.english: four hundred parsa by four hundred parsa.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה שָׁם זָקֵן אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה מַכִּיר בְּחׇכְמַת יְוָונִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's story from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the old man's advice, the besiegers sent up a pig instead of a תמיד, and the land shook.

steps.title: The curses, and the link back to the משנה
steps.stepSummary: After this, the חכמים cursed anyone who raises pigs and anyone who teaches his son חכמת יוונית. The ברייתא then says that the משנה's מעשה, the עומר from גגות צריפין and the שתי הלחם from בקעת עין סוכר, happened at that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time they said: cursed is the one who raises pigs, and cursed is the one who teaches his son Greek wisdom. And about that time we learned in the משנה: the עומר came from גגות צריפין and the שתי הלחם came from the valley of עין סוכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the story with two curses. Then it ties the story to our משנה: the מעשה of the faraway עומר happened during this war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the point of the whole story for our sugya. The משנה said the עומר should come from near ירושלים, but may come from anywhere if that is not possible. The war is the time when they had to bring it from a faraway place.

keyTerms.meaning: The valley of עין סוכר, where the wheat for the שתי הלחם came from in this story

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's story of the עומר from גגות צריפין happened during the חשמונאי civil war. This was the time when they could not follow the best practice of bringing it from near ירושלים.

phrases.english: At that time they said:
Cursed is one who raises pigs,
and cursed is one who teaches his son Greek wisdom.
And about that time we learned:
phrases.notes: "We learned" means in our משנה, the line from step 3.

phrases.english: There was an incident where the omer came from Gaggot Tzerifin,
and the two loaves from the valley of Ein Sokher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story from steps 7 and 8 and connects it back to the משנה's מעשה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's מעשה of the עומר from גגות צריפין happened during the חשמונאי civil war, and at that time the חכמים cursed raising pigs and teaching חכמת יוונית.

steps.title: How they found the place called גגות צריפין
steps.stepSummary: A second story tells how they found the place. They did not know where to get the עומר, so they made an announcement. A חרש pointed one hand at a roof and one at a hut, and מרדכי understood that he meant a place called גגות צריפין. They checked and found it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the time for the עומר came, they did not know where to bring it from. They announced it publicly. A deaf-mute came and put one hand on a roof and his other hand on a hut. מרדכי said to them: is there a place called 'גגות צריפין' or 'צריפין גגות'? They checked and found it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story about the same time. It explains how they discovered the faraway place where the עומר came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nearby fields could not be used, and nobody knew where to get barley. The חרש could not speak, so he gave a hint with his hands: roof (גג) and hut (צריף). מרדכי turned that hint into a place name, and it proved correct.
steps.whatToRemember: The name גגות צריפין was found through a hint: the חרש pointed to a roof (גג) and a hut (צריף), and מרדכי understood it as a place name.

phrases.english: When the time of the omer arrived,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי מֵהֵיכָא אַיְיתִי עוֹמֶר.
phrases.english: they did not know from where to bring the omer.
They made a public announcement.
A certain deaf-mute came,
and placed one hand on a roof
phrases.notes: A roof is a גג and a hut is a צריף, so together his hands spelled out the hint גגות צריפין.

phrases.english: and his other hand on a hut.
Mordekhai said to them:
Is there a place whose name is "Gaggot Tzerifin"
or "Tzerifin Gaggot"?
They checked and found it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא עוֹמֶר, לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי מֵהֵיכָא אַיְיתִי עוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second story about the same time, explaining how they found the place named in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They found the place גגות צריפין through the hint of a חרש, which מרדכי understood, and they brought the עומר from there.

steps.title: A deaf-mute's hint leads them to the wheat for the two loaves
steps.stepSummary: They did not know where to get wheat for the שתי הלחם. A חרש pointed to his eye and to a door latch, and מרדכי figured out that he meant a place called עין סוכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they needed to bring the שתי הלחם, they did not know where to bring it from, so they made an announcement. A deaf-mute came and put one hand on his eye and one hand on a door latch. מרדכי said: Is there a place called עין סוכר or סוכר עין? They checked and found it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story that matches the עומר story from Step 10. This time the problem is finding wheat for the שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as before. There is a public announcement, a חרש answers only with hand signs, and מרדכי turns the signs into a place name. 'Eye' is עין, and the door latch, סיכרא, sounds like סוכר. Put together, they make עין סוכר, the place the משנה named.

keyTerms.meaning: A door latch or bolt; it sounds like סוכר
The place named in the משנה where the wheat came from

steps.whatToRemember: Both the עומר and the שתי הלחם were found through a deaf-mute's hand signs, and both times מרדכי decoded them.

phrases.english: When they needed to bring the two loaves,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי מֵהֵיכָא לְאֵתוֹיֵי, אַכְרוּז.
phrases.english: they did not know where to bring it from, so they made an announcement.
phrases.notes: This is during the siege from Step 7, when the usual fields could not be reached.

phrases.english: A certain deaf-mute man came,
placed his hand on his eye
and one hand on a door latch.
phrases.notes: סיכרא, a latch, sounds like סוכר. That sound is the clue.

phrases.english: מרדכי said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִיכָּא דּוּכְתָּא דִּשְׁמֵהּ ״עֵין סוֹכֵר״ אוֹ ״סוֹכֵר עַיִן״?
phrases.english: Is there a place called 'Ein Sokher' or 'Sokher Ayin'?
They checked and found it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to Step 10: the עומר story, now told for the שתי הלחם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The place for the שתי הלחם wheat, עין סוכר, was found by decoding a deaf-mute's signs.

steps.title: Three women bring bird offerings with unclear explanations
steps.stepSummary: Three women each brought a pair of birds. Each one explained her offering with a single short word: זיבתי, ימתי, עונתי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three women brought three pairs of birds. One said: 'For my זיבה.' One said: 'For my ימה.' One said: 'For my עונה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins another story about מרדכי's wisdom. This step only sets up the puzzle: three women and three unclear words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is short and can be read more than one way. The type of offering each woman owes depends on what she really meant. The next two steps give two different readings.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of birds (doves or pigeons) brought as offerings
A flow, as in the bleeding of a זבה

phrases.english: There were these three women
who brought three pairs of birds.
One said: 'For my ziva.'
And one said: 'For my yamma.'
phrases.notes: This word is connected to ים, which can mean the sea. Keep that in mind for Step 14.

phrases.english: And one said: 'For my ona.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים דְּאַיְיתוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ קִינִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, also showing מרדכי's understanding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three women brought bird offerings, each with a one-word explanation that was unclear.

steps.title: The חכמים first read all three as זבות owing a חטאת and an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים understood each word as describing a woman who had bleeding as a זבה. A זבה brings one bird as a חטאת and one as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: 'זיבתי' means she was truly a זבה; 'ימתי' means truly a flow; 'עונתי' refers to her time. So each one owes one חטאת and one עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first reading of the women's words. This reading sets up מרדכי's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים took all three words as referring to bleeding. If so, each woman is a זבה and owes the required pair: one חטאת and one עולה. This matters a lot, because a חטאת can only be brought when it is truly owed.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who had bleeding outside her normal period and must bring an offering
A sin offering, here the required bird of a זבה
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the final answer. It is the first assumption, and מרדכי overturns it in the next step.

phrases.english: They understood from this:
'My ziva' means she was an actual זבה;
'For my yamma' means actually my flow;
'For my ona' means for her set time;
so for all of them, one is a sin offering and one is a burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first interpretation of the three women's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first reading: all three are זבות, each owing one חטאת and one עולה.

steps.title: מרדכי shows each woman was thanking for being saved, so all are עולות
steps.stepSummary: מרדכי suggested that each woman had been in danger: one through a flow, one at sea, one through her eye. So none owed a חטאת, and all the birds were עולות. They checked, and he was right.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרדכי said to them: Maybe one was in danger through a flow, maybe one was in danger at sea, maybe one was in danger through her eye. If so, all of them are burnt offerings. They checked and found it was so.
steps.whatsHappening: מרדכי rejects the חכמים' reading from Step 13 and offers a better one. Checking with the women proves him right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרדכי reads each word as the cause of a danger, not as a state of impurity: זוב is a dangerous flow, ים is the sea, and עונה hints at עין, her eye. A woman offering birds for being saved is bringing a gift, not paying a required חטאת. So all six birds should be עולות, and the result was confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: They checked and found it to be so

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים thought the women owed a חטאת and an עולה. מרדכי showed they were thanking for being saved, so all the birds were עולות, and checking proved him right.
steps.whyThisMatters: Bringing a חטאת when none is owed is a serious problem. מרדכי's careful reading kept the offerings from being brought the wrong way.

phrases.english: מרדכי said to them:

perhaps she was in danger at sea;
perhaps she was in danger through her eye;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of Step 13 and replaces it with the correct one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole assumption that the three women were זבות owing a חטאת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words could just as well mean each woman was saved from danger, which calls only for עולות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three women's birds were עולות, and checking confirmed מרדכי's reading.
